p: A vertical video ad for Artifact Share demonstrating the workflow of sharing an AI-written spec doc, adding a comment directly on the web page, using a CLI agent command to apply feedback, and viewing the resolved updates at the same URL.
Artifact Share lets teams collaborate on AI-generated design specs at a single URL where agents can read comments and republish updates.

Who reviews it?'"},{"timestamp":"00:05.000","observation":"User highlights text on the shared spec and adds an inline comment."},{"timestamp":"00:12.000","observation":"Terminal screen shows Claude Code CLI processing the review comment."},{"timestamp":"00:17.200","observation":"Updated spec document renders reflecting the 3-week timeline cut."},{"timestamp":"00:23.200","observation":"Clean final end card displays core value proposition and URL CTA."}]

The video effectively outlines the developer workflow from web review to agent CLI integration. Visual elements and text stay legible at small mobile viewports with clean, deliberate pacing. Transitioning between light doc views and a dark terminal slightly impacts continuity, but the overarching demonstration remains focused and clear.

p: ["weak scroll-stopping hook: frame 0 opens with a dense decision doc rather than a punchy line or visual surprise","hook copy diverges from brief (no 'your agent wrote the spec, who reviews it' framing)","wordmark/badge absent in the final CTA frame, breaking 'wordmark every beat' concept","topic drift in beat 4 ('3 weeks. Decided.') toward budget/decision automation, diluting the comment-then-agent-edits throughline"]

The ad's core loop (comment on doc -> CLI agent applies edit -> doc republishes at same URL) is demonstrated concretely and is genuinely the product's differentiator, giving it real product clarity. But the opening frame is a busy, text-heavy mock document rather than a hook built to stop a scrolling developer, so early retention is likely weak. The closing CTA line matches the brief closely and is legible, though it drops the wordmark that appears in every other beat. Net effect: a credible, plausible product demo that under-indexes on hook strength relative to the stated creative intent.
